why: SA5011's remaining entry here is the *missing* one (sa5011/ok/ok.go:89) — upstream reports it and guff does not; the two sigma directions guff now models (`sigma_shadows`, and `renamed_before_check` added 2026-08-13, which closed both consul allowlist entries) are about *not* reporting; SA6001 recall; SA4015/SA4031/SA5005/SA9004 precision. The Go stdlib error text that used to head this list is gone: SA1000, SA1001, SA1002 and SA1007 are all ports now, in crates/guff-staticcheck/src/gostd/. SA1011's recall is gone from this list too (missing 9 -> 7, 2026-08-10): it asked whether a constant was valid UTF-8 while the constant layer held it as Rust text, so the answer was always yes. SA9008's pattern matches upstream exactly; what remains there is its IR verification (docs/COMPAT-HARDENING.md §4, 2026-08-09). SA1019 left this list on 2026-08-12 (missing 7 -> 5, extra 9 -> 7): it reported at the selected name instead of the start of the selector (upstream hands `report.Report` the whole `*ast.SelectorExpr`), and the deprecation message was trimmed while upstream's `strings.Replace(alt, "\\n", " ", -1)` leaves the trailing space that `doc.Text()` puts there. SA4006's interface-boxing extra left this list on 2026-08-13 (extra 7 -> 6): guff-ssa's `MakeInterface` now carries the boxed value, so `i = n` into an `interface{}` gives `n` a referrer. SA1023 and SA4020 left this list on 2026-08-14 (missing 5 -> 3, extra 6 -> 4): SA1023 reported at the function name and once per function, where upstream reports the modifying *instruction* — the assignment, or the `append` call itself — once each; SA4020 spelled the empty-interface case "earlier case" instead of naming the type as written (`any` vs `interface{}`). Both measured against golangci-lint 2.12.2. 2026-08-14, second pass: SA4015 was inverted — its IR arm matched `ChangeType` where upstream matches `ir.Convert`, so it had zero recall, and the AST fallback standing in for it fired on `math.Ceil(1)`, which upstream never reports (the constant is already float64, there is no conversion). Rewritten to the IR arm alone; 7 shapes now match golangci-lint 2.12.2 exactly. SA9004 reported at the group's type expression instead of `group[0].Pos()`, i.e. the first name. The two survivors are SA4031 and SA5005, and both are inverted the same way as SA4015 was: measured on 2026-08-14, upstream reports 5 shapes of SA4031 (make/new/slice-literal/func-value/address-of, with related information naming the variable) and guff reports none of them while reporting an inline `make(chan int) == nil` upstream ignores; upstream reports SA5005 on *nothing*, including the textbook `runtime.SetFinalizer(x, func(_ *int){ _ = x })`, while guff reports it. Both need a real port, not a tweak. SA4031 was ported properly on 2026-08-14 (extra 2 -> 1): it walks `*ast.IfStmt` only — a bare `make(chan int) == nil` is not a finding — proves the operand never-nil by walking the IR back through MakeChan/MakeMap/MakeSlice/Alloc/Function/MakeClosure/Slice/FieldAddr/Phi, and hands `&x == nil` to SA4022. That also needed `new(T)` lowered to a heap Alloc in guff-ssa, which it was not. All 5 shapes now match golangci-lint 2.12.2. The one survivor is SA5005, and it is not a defect in the check: guff now implements upstream's exact conditions (a Load of an Alloc, a MakeClosure, and a binding equal to that Alloc), and guff's IR satisfies them where honnef's does not — honnef reports SA5005 on *nothing*, including the example in its own documentation. Recorded as an architectural difference, not a bug; upstream's `(at %s)` message suffix is left off because no upstream finding exists to compare with. 2026-08-14, third pass — the counts did not move, but two of the golden's entries are new. SA4019 and SA4032 had never been compared: both fixtures were `linux`-only, so `go list` dropped them on the darwin machine every golden here was recorded on, and CI reported guff's two findings as extras (darwin missing 3 / extra 1, linux missing 3 / extra 3, same commit and same binary). The fixtures now carry `!plan9`, which resolves the same way on all four supported platforms, and `compat/golden/platforms.py` refuses any case that reintroduces the axis. Comparing SA4032 for the first time found two real defects, both fixed here: it reported at the operator where upstream hands the whole `BinaryExpr` to `report.Report`, and it accepted either operand order and any string constant where upstream's pattern pins the symbol left and a `BasicLit` right. SA4019 matched on sight. Neither check is on this list.
